title: CHAMP: Cross-domain Hybrid Architecture for Matchmaking and Prediction in Online Multi-Player Games
abstract: arXiv:2609.04870v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multiplayer Online Battle Arena (MOBA) games rely on matchmaking to maintain competitive balance. Our prior work, CUPID, framed matchmaking as an assignment re-optimization problem and showed that a single-mode win-rate predictor can meaningfully rebalance teams. However, deploying such a system across diverse player populations exposes three practical bottlenecks: most queueing players lack sufficient in-mode match history (cold start), skill distributions shift drastically across rank tiers (distribution inconsistency), and extreme skill segments are severely data-starved. translated_title: CHAMP：面向在线多人游戏匹配与预测的跨领域混合架构
translated_abstract: 多人在线战术竞技（MOBA）游戏依赖匹配系统来维持竞技平衡。我们先前的工作CUPID将匹配问题建模为分配再优化问题，并证明单一模式的胜率预测器能够有效地重新平衡队伍。然而，将此类系统部署到多样化的玩家群体中会暴露出三个实际瓶颈：大多数排队玩家缺乏足够的同模式对局历史（冷启动问题）、技能分布在各个段位之间剧烈变化（分布不一致问题），以及极端技能水平的玩家群体严重缺乏数据。我们提出了CHAMP，一个解决这些部署瓶颈的跨领域匹配框架。为了解决数据稀疏和冷启动问题，CHAMP用混合领域特征收集方式取代了仅使用目标模式的玩家画像：即一个按时间戳排序的跨模式短期序列，其切片标注了目标领域特征，外加每种模式的（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: CHAMP提出了一个跨领域匹配框架，通过混合领域特征（跨模式短期序列加目标领域特征标注）解决MOBA游戏匹配系统部署中的冷启动、段位间分布不一致和极端段位数据稀缺三大瓶颈。
en_tdlr: CHAMP presents a cross-domain matchmaking framework that uses hybrid domain features (cross-mode short-term sequences annotated with target-domain features) to resolve three deployment bottlenecks in MOBA game matchmaking: cold start, distribution inconsistency across rank tiers, and data scarcity at extreme skill segments.
